jbtxHHpX_u0.title: 20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying
jbtxHHpX_u0.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
jbtxHHpX_u0.summary: In '20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying' (published 27 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA argues Meta's new Muse personal AI agent is the first real killer app for agentic AI — bringing agents to consumer spending — and maps the ~20 stocks it upends. He likes PayPal (bought back at ~$50 after the takeover-offer rejection cratered it; ~10x P/E vs 16x a year ago, stablecoin growth) and Shopify (Muse users find its merchants' products and check out via Shop Pay; the rails underneath if Muse becomes shopping's front door) as the 'winners to buy'. Expedia is a conditional rebound play: its Muse partnership could redirect bookings through Expedia at Booking's expense, and the stock trades at 16x earnings vs a 25x average — though he stays cautious on the whole travel-middleman group (TripAdvisor, Airbnb, Booking, -15% to -24% in a month). On the AI-build side he ranks four neo-clouds — Oracle, Nebius, CoreWeave, IREN — and takes another look only at Nebius (his pick): ~500% revenue growth, best debt-to-free-cash-flow (-1.8x), 9.8x growth-adjusted P/S — while flagging Oracle's force majeure on a 2.5GW New Mexico data center as 'the first crack in the entire AI boom'. He avoids brokerages (Schwab, Raymond James, LPL, Ameriprise), banks (BofA, JPMorgan) and insurers (Progressive, Allstate) — AI agents could replace advice fees and erode sticky deposit-sweep profits — plus subscription names exposed to AI-driven cancellations (Adobe, SiriusXM, Match, Peloton, Planet Fitness, crushed 15%). Meta itself he holds: great story but ~30% above its 5-year average valuation after the 30% three-week run. Other tickers discussed with no call: Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, Salesforce, ServiceNow, AppLovin, Amazon. Caption note: auto-captions garble 'CoreWeave' as 'Corvus', 'IREN' as 'Iron', and 'Marvell' as 'Marvel'; tickers here are corrected.

7Lm8O0CuvLs.title: AMD Just Spent $8.2 Billion on Its Next AI Bet!!
7Lm8O0CuvLs.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
7Lm8O0CuvLs.summary: In 'AMD Just Spent $8.2 Billion on Its Next AI Bet!!' (published 29 Sep 2026), Jose Najarro covers two big semiconductor headlines. First, Nvidia increased its share-repurchase authorization by $150 billion, bringing the remaining buyback program to $235 billion to be executed through fiscal 2028 — against barely $100 billion of buybacks over the past decade. He reads it as a major confidence signal: management believes the money will be worth much more in the future, and the stock trades at roughly 19x forward earnings (likely 16-17x, he argues, since analysts keep underestimating Nvidia's growth). He also covers Nvidia's open agent safety platform — an open-source OpenShell runtime plus a Sentry watchdog running on Bluefield 4 DPUs — and notes partners include Anthropic, SpaceX and Perplexity, with OpenAI conspicuously absent. He reports Anthropic has contracted 2.6 gigawatts of Nvidia AI infrastructure to date, with partner contracted value exceeding $180 billion, dismissing fears Anthropic is moving away from Nvidia. Second, AMD's $8.2 billion all-stock acquisition of World Labs, the AI model and research lab founded by AI pioneer Dr. Fei-Fei Li (auto-captions garble her name as 'FFly'/'Dr. Lee'), expected to close by end of 2026. He frames it as a talent acquisition that gives AMD a front-row view of how AI workloads are evolving, informing its hardware/software roadmap and potential moves into robotics and physical AI. He applauds the all-stock structure — less than 1% of the company — as smarter than spending cash, while flagging one worry: AMD is already juggling software-stack improvements (ROCm), the Helios ramp, and a full-stack build-out, so this is one more thing on the plate. He trusts Lisa Su's judgment and expects the deal to look obviously smart in a year or two. Calls: NVDA — BUY (excited as an investor; buyback confidence; cheap forward P/E; $5T market cap noted); AMD — BUY (smart talent grab, trusts management; ~$67 per garbled captions). Other tickers discussed without calls: INTC and ARM (as compute platforms for the agent safety runtime), META (as an AMD partner), plus non-tradeable OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX and Perplexity.

gkt3BnXJf9s.summary: Joseph Hogue, CFA — 'My New Favorite Stocks for AI Growth AND Income' (published 29 Sep 2026). Pitch: income investors no longer have to choose between AI-driven growth and cash flow. Hogue argues new YieldMax option-income ETFs let holders capture semiconductor upside while converting industry volatility into distributions. He walks through four: (1) CHPY — YieldMax Semiconductor Portfolio Options Income ETF, holding 15-30 semiconductor names and using a call-spread strategy targeting ~40% annualized distribution with weekly payouts (range this year $0.38-$0.71/share). (2) SOXY — the YieldMax Target 12 semiconductor fund, a growth-leaning counterpart targeting 12% income so more upside stays in the portfolio (monthly payouts, $0.65 to over $1/share this year). (3) AMDY — a single-stock AMD options-income ETF for a tactical overweight on AMD, which he says he bought early last year and has since cashed. (4) NVDY — the single-stock Nvidia version targeting a 47% distribution rate. Suggested builds: max income = 70% CHPY / 15% NVDY / 15% AMDY; income-plus-growth = 50% SOXY / 25% AMDY / 25% NVDY. He flags the risks: distributions fluctuate with premiums and volatility, and income is never guaranteed. Calls made: CHPY BUY (~40% target), SOXY BUY (12% target), AMDY BUY, NVDY BUY (47% target). Other tickers discussed: MU (up ~1,200% over 5 years), MRVL (~+400%), NVDA (10x), ARM — all mentioned only as semiconductor theme leaders held inside the ETFs, not as direct calls. Note: captions rendered the second fund's ticker as 'SOX Y', with garbled repeats as 'SOXW' and 'SOXL' later in the video — the described product is consistently the Target 12 fund. The video is sponsored by YieldMax, disclosed in-video.

_X0c2A-Ln9c.summary: Travis Hoeft (Asymmetric Investing) — 'Risk Warning: 5 Stocks to Sell Before It's Too Late' (published 29 Sep 2026). Core thesis: five of the market's most popular AI-related stocks are vastly overvalued, and their improved financials are a mirage because AI capex doesn't hit the income statement until assets are in use. The common thread is deteriorating credit: borrowing costs are rising both market-wide and company-specific, execution is stumbling, and debt markets could eventually close to these names. (1) ORCL SELL — Oracle is down 53% over the past year; trailing-12-month free cash flow is -$28B against nearly $120B of debt, the 10-year borrowing rate has risen from 5.7% in February to ~7.3%, and the Project Jupiter data center invoking force majeure is 'not normal' — a sign of real execution problems behind $664B of remaining performance obligations. (2) CRWV SELL — CoreWeave carries a $47B market cap on just $7.6B of trailing revenue, $35B of debt, and burned -$5.7B of free cash flow in Q2 2026 alone; its June 2026 8.5% notes now yield over 12%, ROIC is negative. (3) MU SELL — take profits on Micron ($1.2T market cap): the ~7x forward P/E looks cheap only if 83-86% gross margins hold, but memory is a commodity — capacity lands in 2028-29, chip designs are shifting away from expensive HBM, and margin reversion to 40% would wipe out ~90% of profits. (4) AMZN SELL — retail growth has slowed (~13% TTM) and its $39B of retail operating profit is essentially the advertising business, which is threatened by agentic AI shopping (Muse/ChatGPT buy without viewing ads); estimated -$34B free cash flow in 2026, 26x forward P/E. (5) TSLA SELL — revenue flat for three years, operating margins down to 2-4.2% (a regular automaker), trading at 13x sales / 192x forward earnings, with ~$26B of capex expected to exceed operating cash flow, while Musk's attention shifts to SpaceX. Notable: two days after Joseph Hogue rated ORCL and CRWV AVOID on this same watch, Hoeft escalates both to outright SELL. Captions render CoreWeave as 'Cororeweave' throughout — ticker CRWV confirmed against the company discussed.

sY9DIuxZzmc.title: Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock
sY9DIuxZzmc.creator: Daniel Pronk
sY9DIuxZzmc.summary: In 'Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock' (published 30 Sep 2026), Daniel Pronk returns from two weeks in Italy to reassure viewers asking whether Meta's ~30% rally from the lows has made it expensive. His answer: no — his DCF still shows a $827 fair value on conservative inputs (15% annual operating-cash-flow growth, 14x price/OCF) and ~$1,000 on realistic ones (20% growth, 15x OCF, still below the 16x historical median), implying 15-22.6% annualized returns over three years. The video's first half is a long showcase of Meta's new Muse AI agent: over 3 million US downloads in 9 days, #1 on the App Store for two weeks, adopted faster than ChatGPT, and Pronk's own daily use cases — sponsorship email triage, media kits, and home-purchase paperwork, all via email access. He argues Muse rides Meta's free distribution across Instagram and WhatsApp, and its clearest monetization is harvesting user data to sharpen ad targeting. He is skeptical of Zuckerberg's 'savings-shared' monetization model (Muse touches no transaction) and unconvinced agentic AI will fully disrupt Amazon/Booking.com advertising — window-shopping behavior persists. On Meta Connect: Muse at the center, the teased 'watermelon' frontier model, impressive new VR glasses, and a questionable Meta Charm pocket device. Call: META — BUY (adding), still undervalued at ~23x next year's earnings; he will add when post-house-closing liquidity frees up. No other tickers called.

989CUhoOUg8.title: Buffett's "Going to Hell" Warning [5 Stocks to Buy Before It Gets Worse]
989CUhoOUg8.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
989CUhoOUg8.summary: In 'Buffett's "Going to Hell" Warning [5 Stocks to Buy Before It Gets Worse]' (published 30 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA frames a Warren Buffett warning about part of the market 'going to hell' around the 10-year Treasury hitting a 24-year high. He attributes surging rates to four forces: persistent inflation (gas-driven CPI +3.4%), Uncle Sam's $2 trillion deficit, an AI-debt boom (Goldman sees hyperscaler debt issuance at a record $420B next year), and unexpectedly strong economic growth (flash PMI at a 5-year high) forcing the Fed toward more hikes. Five stocks to buy for this regime: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) — ~$360B in cash and T-bills collecting tens of billions at high rates, with financials/insurers in its portfolio earning more interest income; CME and CBOE — both down up to 17% last month on prediction-market competition fears, beneficiaries of rate-uncertainty hedging volume with a near-term bounce coming; the VanEck gold miners ETF (GDX) as a safety bet on inflation, deficits, and dollar weakness; and Vanguard's long-term bond ETF (BLV) — a conditional buy ("a little early"), attractive once rates level off, with a ~5% dividend and a possible bounce to $70 in the next recession. Six stocks to avoid: high-debt JBLU (debt/equity 591%, negative operating cash flow) and CCL (down 26% YTD, a falling knife), plus housing-chain DHI, PHM, BLDR, and Z as mortgage rates top 7%. Notable stance flip: Bank of America (BAC) moves from AVOID (Sep 28, long-term AI threat to financials) to BUY here — Hogue explicitly splits the time horizon: rate income now, AI disruption later. Sponsored Kalshi per-futures segment and a note that he is 'deeply invested in Ethereum' are mentions, not calls.

Ad2Pn32TWSs.title: Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!
Ad2Pn32TWSs.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
Ad2Pn32TWSs.summary: In 'Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!' (published 1 Oct 2026, covering Micron's Sep 30 post-close print), Jose Najarro — who does not own the stock — argues the triple beat (revenue, EPS, and next-quarter guidance all well above consensus) leaves Micron cheap, with the flat after-hours reaction reflecting already-high hopes. His bull case: pricing is doing the heavy lifting (DRAM revenue +27% YoY, NAND +42%, on only mid-single-digit bit growth), and Micron expects a tight market through 2027-28 even with mid-20s industry bit-shipment growth; 35% of revenue through 2030 is covered by multi-year take-or-pay contracts, with $150B of remaining performance obligations (at minimum contract prices, so the real figure could be much higher) and $32B in customer cash deposits. HBM repricing begins at the start of calendar 2027, Q1 is the gross-margin floor, and buybacks unlock after December 9 (the CHIPS Act incentive 2-year anniversary) — he would not be surprised by a $50B repurchase authorization. Watch items: DRAM sequential price growth is decelerating (from ~60% to the high teens), consumer PC/phone units face double-digit declines in 2026, and capex is stepping up past $50B in 2027 (funded by contracted demand, he stresses). Caveat: auto-captions heavily garble the reported figures (e.g. '$54.2 billion in revenue', '$33 in one quarter' EPS, '$60 to 63 billion' guide) — treat all numbers here as approximate. Call: MU — BUY ('still dirt cheap'), with a rerating as the prize and supply-tight AI demand as the engine. Also bullish on the wider semiconductor/neocloud space as a memory bottleneck 'extends the cycle'.

WHzxbGZoTPQ.title: Unloved Chinese Stocks - Value, Buy for 2X?
WHzxbGZoTPQ.creator: Sven Carlin
WHzxbGZoTPQ.summary: Sven Carlin works through the ~20 largest holdings of the China internet ETF - unloved after 13 years with no performance - screening for value: low P/Es, high cash flows, profitability and growth. Tencent (P/E ~15, dividends, buybacks, double-digit growth) is "interesting" on his buy-the-bad-mood/sell-the-exuberance framework; he owns Prosus as his Tencent proxy. JD.com he owns outright - the investment/profitability cycle swings 50-70%, with very high cash flow per share, dividend, 3.7% buyback yield and a logistics moat. Kuaishou is his standout free bet: core business at P/E ~7 with 68% ownership of Kling AI (raised ~$3B, growing 200%). Baidu trades near book value of its cash with AI/robotaxi optionality; Trip.com at P/E 10 with ~RMB 14B cash looks interesting; Tencent Music is cheap and profitable. Alibaba is "too high now" on declining legacy cash flows; NetEase and Lenovo are fairly priced holds. He avoids KE Holdings (P/E 26, frozen transaction market), Bilibili, GDS and Kingsoft Cloud. Overall: buy big-cap Chinese internet on weakness for ~50% minimum over three years, hold via ETF or directly, size ~10-15% of a global value portfolio - and only for European investors; he explicitly warns US investors off due to sanction/illiquidity risk (VIE structure, Taiwan). Note: auto-captions garble several names (Meituan as "Mu1", Kling AI as "Cling AI", renminbi as "raimi/remimi") - treat P/E and cash figures as approximate.

F6ds1vqtOTY.title: A Once in a Lifetime Financial Reset is Coming. (Why Stocks Are Next)
F6ds1vqtOTY.creator: Tom Nash
F6ds1vqtOTY.summary: Tom Nash reframes the "market crash is coming" narrative: a crash is certain, but the wrong question is 'will it crash?' - the right ones are whether your portfolio is protected and set up to profit from it. He walks through historical playbooks (1973 oil embargo, 1990 Iraq war, 2022 Ukraine) showing crashes followed by multi-year recoveries, and the volatility stats that make staying invested work (54% of days, 75% of years, 95% of decades, 100% of 20-year periods positive). His system: 12-month emergency fund, kill expensive debt, max tax-advantaged accounts, zero leverage, then a portfolio stress test using beta (a 50/50 S&P/Palantir portfolio falls ~60% in a 30% S&P drop). Stock selection: a big S&P 500 core as the "undefeated cheat code", elite businesses run through a 125-point scorecard, max 10 positions, dollar-cost average and double down on the way down (he bought Palantir at $6-9 in 2022). Emotions are the portfolio killer: 24-hour cooldown rule, don't check daily, write a personal "constitution". No explicit stock calls - Palantir, Tesla and Nvidia appear only as high-beta stress-test examples; the actionable recommendation is SPY as the core holding. Ends with a pitch for his free "panic-proof guide" and the academy (patreon.com/theMASH).

HWGUIaBgdd4.title: [BUY HEAVY!] THIS ONE Stock Runs the Sports Economy
HWGUIaBgdd4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
HWGUIaBgdd4.summary: In '[BUY HEAVY!] THIS ONE Stock Runs the Sports Economy' (published 2 Oct 2026), Joseph Hogue follows up on his earlier Genius Sports video, arguing the market still prices GENI as a narrow sports-betting data vendor while it is becoming the critical infrastructure layer of the $100B+ sports economy. He lays out five pillars: sportsbooks (Genius supplies official real-time data, streaming and trading tech into a $111B global betting market); leagues and teams (NFL, Premier League, NCAA partnerships turn games into monetizable digital products; PWC sees team valuations accelerating); broadcasters and the advertising layer (live game data plus the fan-graph/moments engine won 174 new advertisers in Q2, incl. McDonald's, Airbnb and YouTube TV; the Legend acquisition adds 320M+ annual visits); and prediction markets, where Genius already partners with Kalshi and Polymarket as trusted arbiter (their combined volume rose ~5x in 7 months). These reinforce each other as a flywheel. On valuation he stays near-term conservative: $12/share from 2026E $1.02B revenue at his 5-year average 3.2x P/S, then argues ~$20/share (~270% upside from under $6) if 2027 sales reach ~$1.4B and the stock re-rates to 4x sales (2024 level). He flags the bear case honestly: rising league-rights renewal costs, competition from Sportradar, and that the flywheel must convert into sustained cash flow (guidance: 60% FCF conversion by 2028). Call: GENI BUY.

4e4bnSjMDsg.title: The 10x Stock I'm Loading Up On This Month
4e4bnSjMDsg.creator: Asymmetric Investing
4e4bnSjMDsg.summary: In 'The 10x Stock I'm Loading Up On This Month' (published 2 Oct 2026), Travis Hoeft reveals his October buy for the Asymmetric (ACE Metro) portfolio: Zillow (Z), which he is buying as a 10x-over-10-years compounder despite the stock being down 61% over the past year. His four-part checklist — revenue growth, margin expansion, multiple expansion, buybacks — is, he argues, all present. Revenue is growing 17.7% and accelerating even in a weak housing market, driven by rentals ($734M TTM, +34% CAGR) and the mortgage leg rather than the traditional 8%-growth residential business; the company now positions itself as where people answer all housing questions, an aggregator that owns customer demand. Operating margin flipped from -13.5% (Mar-2024 quarter) to slightly positive, with $258M TTM free cash flow and ~$800M of recent buybacks shrinking shares from ~242M. Valuation looks unloved: ~11x forward P/E, ~15x forward P/FCF, 2.2x sales. His main criticism is stock-based compensation (still $363M, down from $423M) and he admits the housing market could get worse short-term, but sees that as the launching pad. Note: this is a cross-creator divergence — Joseph Hogue had Z as AVOID on 30 Sep on housing-supply-chain weakness. Call: Z BUY.

jAtRNbIWaOw.title: NVIDIA Just Changed the AI Market AGAIN — Here's What Comes Next
jAtRNbIWaOw.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
jAtRNbIWaOw.summary: In 'NVIDIA Just Changed the AI Market AGAIN — Here's What Comes Next' (published 4 Oct 2026), Jose Najarro walks through a week of Nvidia news he calls one 'oh snap' and several bullish moments. The 'oh snap': Nvidia's 1 Oct blog showing GPT-6 Astra running on Blackwell at up to 18x faster token generation undercuts the speed-moat story of Cerebras (CBRS, +~20% in five days pre-news), whose OpenAI ultra-fast partnership now looks exposed — though he says it is too early to call it game over and notes Altman's reassuring partnership comments as mildly bullish for Cerebras. Bullish for Nvidia: stock ~$238 (all-time high, ~$5.7T market cap, +23% YTD), OpenAI's Dots agentic AI driving more token consumption (he sees the supply/demand imbalance lasting through ~Oct 2028), and AWS raising GPU prices ~15% from 2 Oct (B300/B200, H100/H200, A100) as evidence demand still outstrips supply. He also reinforces his 1 Oct post-earnings MU BUY: the new 64GB DGX Spark at ~$5,000 (half the memory of the $4,000 128GB original, now $7,000) shows memory pricing is 'insane' and the shortage persists; Pixel 10a's $100 price hike is memory-driven too. Other names: neoclouds and hyperscalers broadly bullish, no specific calls; Cerebras discussed at length but no call (captions garble it as Cerebrus/soas/surreal shareholder). Calls: NVDA BUY (bullish continuation), MU BUY (thesis reinforced).

Zrbf8mXwsG4.title: I Rank the 7 Best Stocks to Buy Right Now October 2026
Zrbf8mXwsG4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
Zrbf8mXwsG4.summary: Joseph Hogue's weekly update (published 4 Oct) argues market concentration is the whole story: the nine largest S&P 500 stocks added 13.5% while the index itself is only up 13% YTD, meaning the other 491 stocks contributed nothing. The common thread is AI — 'the only game in town' at this point in the bull market — but this late in the cycle you must be picky. He walks through five AI segments and names seven stocks he is buying now: ServiceNow and Palantir in software (agentic orchestration theme, cheap PEGs), Nvidia and Broadcom in infrastructure (0.48x PEG and best data-center exposure), Zscaler and Fortinet in cybersecurity (cheapest PEGs in an expensive group), and Bloom Energy in power (0.44x PEG, colocated generation). He owns and is holding Palo Alto and CrowdStrike but calls them too expensive to add; Oracle is the one name he says to 'definitely avoid' over the neo-cloud crack-up. Nebius and CoreWeave soften to waits. He also warns of an 'October surprise': September oil near $100 will push the 14 Oct CPI up, likely triggering a typical 3-5% dip — don't be all-in, hold cash to buy the dip. Auto-captions garble names heavily (Panw/PAW, Fortnite/FTNT, Zcaler/ZS, Oristrista/ANET, Verdive/VRT); figures treated as approximate.

951xEYynOGo.title: The AI Stock Investors Just Got Another MASSIVE Bull Signal!!
951xEYynOGo.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
951xEYynOGo.summary: Jose Najarro covers Marvell Technology's investor day and Lisa Su's comments from Taipei, arguing both are fresh confirmation of the AI semiconductor demand cycle. Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to about $20 billion (from $18 billion two months earlier, and $16.5 billion before that), with both raises driven by networking -- scale-up/scale-out optics and switching. Custom silicon's FY2029 target is now over $12 billion versus $10 billion-plus reaffirmed in August, and the FY2031 model calls for $70-90 billion in revenue implying over $30 of non-GAAP EPS at the midpoint. On simple math he sketches a $600 potential stock price (30x on $30 CY2030 EPS), stressing it is 4-5 years out and that he would not claim it as a base case. He treats the day as bullish confirmation for his 'ETF approach' trio of Marvell, Credo Technology (dip into the $150s-$160s was a buy, he says; up ~4%) and Astera Labs (up ~8%), and reads Broadcom as the bigger beneficiary given it leads the semi-custom market Marvell is chasing. Su's Taiwan remarks on expanding CPU/GPU production and wafer capacity are framed as another 'brick' in his bullish thesis house, with server CPU revenue guided up over 70% in 2027 and data-center revenue expected to more than double; he notes the server CPU market estimate grew from $60 billion (Nov 2025) to $220 billion. Calls: MRVL BUY (~$600 potential CY2030 model), AMD BUY, AVGO BUY (read-through), CRDO BUY ($150s-$160s dip zone), ALAB BUY. NVDA and MU mentioned only in passing. Caption notes: auto-captions garble Marvell as 'Marll'/'Marvel', Broadcom as 'Broncom', Credo as 'Credto', and Lisa Su as 'Lisa Sue'.

czgmVfoNao4.title: 5 Stocks to Buy BEFORE the 2027 AI Bank Crash
czgmVfoNao4.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
czgmVfoNao4.summary: Joseph Hogue argues AI agents (spurred by Meta's Muse launch, ~3M downloads by late September) will remove the friction that keeps tens of millions of customers in legacy banks paying 0.01-0.04% on deposits, forcing traditional banks into a damned-if-you-do choice: lose deposits or match ~3.5% rates and crater net interest income. His back-of-envelope stress test puts the industry hit at up to $52B, with JPMorgan (a $900B market cap bank paying 0.01%) risking ~$30B of its $95B interest income and Citigroup ~$5.5B. He ranks five legacy banks as avoids - Citigroup, JPMorgan, U.S. Bancorp, Wells Fargo and Bank of America - though he names Bank of America (1.37x book, 0.71x PEG, 8.5% expected revenue growth) the best relative deal of the group if buying the selloff. His five buys are the fintech beneficiaries: SoFi (32% expected revenue growth, 0.69x PEG, "a great deal"), Coinbase (3.5% USDC rewards, tokenization tailwind), Robinhood (31% growth, 2.4x PEG), PayPal (1.4x PEG, slower 4.4% growth but cheap) and Ally Financial (0.85x book, 0.3x PEG, the value pick). He is transparent that the stress test is crude - banks could respond with fees or funding shifts - and that the shift plays out over years, not weeks. Calls: SOFI/COIN/HOOD/PYPL/ALLY BUY (PYPL and ALLY reiterations); C/JPM/USB/WFC/BAC AVOID - BAC is a stance flip from his Oct 1 BUY. The video includes a sponsored Monarch money-app segment.

1Js-3kgdOMw.title: 3 Positive Asymmetric Buys From The Bets Quadrant...
1Js-3kgdOMw.creator: Sven Carlin
1Js-3kgdOMw.summary: Sven Carlin updates the "bets" side of his value-investing quadrant with three positive asymmetric risk/reward ideas, stressing these are bets, not margin-of-safety value investments. On Lululemon he details Michael Burry's tax-loss harvest (bought ~$200, sold everything at a ~50% loss after a one-day rotation into Deckers, likely back in January after the 30-day wash rule) and argues nothing happens for 45-60 days: wait ~3 months, watch for year-end tax-loss selling and the new CEO's likely kitchen-sink first call. His three bets: Kuaishou (P/E 7, 400M daily users, Kling AI IPO next year with Hogue's 68% stake worth ~HKD 12B against a legacy business valued near HKD 4B), Pinduoduo ($107B market cap, $66B cash -> ~4x P/E ex-cash, investing RMB 100B to build a third business), and Charter Communications (~3x free cash flow on an adjusted $16B market cap, a 2x if rates turn but saddled with $120B of refinancing risk). He explicitly rejects Uber ("no Uber for me" - no moat, acquisition-fueled growth), Adobe (slow AI-driven decline), Google ("no way Jose"), Birkenstock (quality deterioration anecdote plus PE ownership change), and Petrobras drilling (squeeze bet he no longer takes). Tencent Music moves from the bets quadrant to his investment quadrant. He walks through Mohnish Pabrai's concentrated bucket bets (Transocean/Valaris rigs, Mark Leonard/Constellation, Turkey, coal, India financials) as idea sources he is mostly too uncomfortable to take, and notes Alibaba only gets interesting below $100 (sold his last at $175). Calls: KUAIS/PDD/CHTR CONDITIONAL_BUY (KUAIS softened from Oct 2 BUY; PDD upgraded from UNCERTAIN); BIRK/UBER/GOOGL/ADBE/PBR AVOID; LULU/BABA UNCERTAIN; KSPI HOLD (owned). Auto-captions garble names (Pabrai as "Pabry", Kling as "Cling", Kuaishou as "Quao").

vFGkr80KPBw.title: ONE Stock is All You Need in This $5 Trillion Opportunity
vFGkr80KPBw.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
vFGkr80KPBw.summary: Hogue frames humanoid robotics as the "$5 trillion opportunity" (Morgan Stanley's estimate of a ~930M-humanoid market by 2050) and pitches Robo Strategy (BOT), a Nasdaq-listed closed-end fund, as the single vehicle giving everyday investors pre-IPO access to private robotics leaders - Figure, Apptronik, Dyna Robotics and Standard Bots - they would otherwise never reach. He walks through the closed-end mechanics investors must understand: the difference between the fund's NAV ($11.35/share as of Aug 31, ~$277M net assets) and its market price, with an illustrative $25 vs $11.35 NAV example showing a 2x+ premium. He stresses it is a long-term, sized position - "not an all-in, all-at-once idea" - and lays out the milestones that matter: pilots converting to production deployments, operating hours and intervention rates, and unit economics (cost per robot, cost per productive hour). His upside framing goes beyond Morgan Stanley: Robo Strategy's own $60T total-addressable-market scenario for robotics plus physical AI. Call: BOT - BUY (first tracked; market price not stated, premium/discount to NAV is the central risk). MU gets only a passing market-cap comparison (his UNCERTAIN stance unchanged); SK Hynix, Sanctuary and the private holdings are passing mentions with no calls. Caption garbles: "Joseph Ogg" for Hogue, "Daina" for Dyna Robotics; a Standard Bots Series C figure is unreliable as captioned.

vAYeWqe9edU.title: 2 Stocks I'm Buying While The Market Panics
vAYeWqe9edU.creator: Daniel Pronk

He closes optimistic with a Bruce Flatt/Howard Marks clip and names the two stocks where the majority of his capital is flowing. Construction Partners (ROAD) - BUY: unjustified selloff after a good Q3 with guidance raised a third time this year, 80-85% of next year's revenue contractually locked, oil/asphalt cost pass-throughs protecting margins, a doubled business by 2030; trading around six-year lows on price-to-EBITDA. RL8-R7QY7jU.title: Why I'm Buying These 3 Stocks (Ignore the AI Hype)
RL8-R7QY7jU.creator: Asymmetric Investing
RL8-R7QY7jU.summary: Travis Hoium pitches his three cheapest current holdings - all trading at single-digit forward multiples he expects to re-rate as growth and margins compound - and says he has been accumulating all three through 2026, rebutting the market's two core fears (autonomous vehicles killing ride-hail, gaming demand peaking). Lyft (LYFT) - BUY: >30M active riders, ~1B rides a year, $1.1B TTM free cash flow, net-cash balance sheet; ~8x forward P/E, ~5x forward P/FCF; the AV-disruption fear is overblown given the Waymo partnership, the European taxi foothold and potential acquirer appeal at this multiple (he would not be surprised if "a Waymo buys them, a Zoox buys them"); his stated bear case is Lyft falling to #4 in autonomy if Tesla and Waymo enter. Uber (UBER) - BUY: gross bookings, trips, monthly riders (28M) and delivery all compounding; mobility CAGR 22%, delivery ~19%; his bull case is Uber as the demand-aggregator for every AV player a decade out. MGM Resorts (MGM) - BUY: EV/EBITDA and P/FCF both below 8x on a $7.5B market cap with ~$1B/year buybacks (~15% of shares); the real catalyst is 2030 MGM Japan in Osaka (~$10B property), where a Marina Bay Sands proxy (~$6B revenue, ~$3B adjusted EBITDA) implies MGM's 44% stake alone could be worth the whole market cap. TgDV_-LeQSE.title: AI Stocks Just Crashed - But Wall Street Missed Something BIG!!

6scmMOSLPM4.title: Are These the Best 5 Growth Stocks to Buy?
6scmMOSLPM4.creator: Asymmetric Investing
6scmMOSLPM4.summary: Asymmetric Investing walks through five growth stocks that are all current holdings in his asymmetric portfolio, arguing they remain long-term compounders after a rough 2026 marked by multiple compression. 1) SoFi (SOFI): shares down 44% but revenue up 41% YoY; lending and financial-services revenue strong, though the technology-platform business weakened after losing Chime as a customer in late 2025. Price-to-book collapsed from ~5 (Sep 2025) to ~1.8, vs big banks at ~2x — the core of the thesis, alongside digital-first scalability and a 35% member CAGR since 2023 (15.8M members, most holding one product, with cross-sell runway). 2) Robinhood (HOOD): down ~29%; maturing from options/crypto 'YOLO' revenue toward net interest and margin revenue, with retirement accounts growing fast and international expansion ahead. Still ~50x earnings and 35x price-to-free-cash-flow; he trimmed a little late last year on stretched valuation but expects 30%+ revenue compounding over a decade. 3) Zeta Global (ZETA): his best 2026 performer (+67%), 34% 3-year revenue CAGR accelerating after the Athena platform launch, operating margin just turning positive; EV/sales ~5, forward P/E ~30. 4) Duolingo (DUOL): contrarian turnaround play, down 56% over the year but up 66% in six months; he dollar-cost-averaged into the position in late 2025 and early 2026. ~18x P/E and 17x P/FCF on 29% revenue growth; engagement (daily active users) is inflecting after 2025 over-monetization hurt growth, and AI tools are expanding product (math, chess) and interactivity. 5) Hims & Hers (HIMS): rough start to 2026 when GLP-1 compounding hit regulatory walls and Novo Nordisk sued, but settled — Novo and Eli Lilly products are now on the platform; management guides 50% revenue growth in H2 2026 after the Eucalyptus/Zava European acquisitions, with EV/sales ~2.8. He frames all five as asymmetric: limited downside, near-unlimited upside. Caption note: auto-generated; 'Dualingo' and 'Himson and Hers' are Duolingo and Hims & Hers; some figures are garbled in places but the five theses are clear.

eKQsjwdRrhA.title: A Once In A 100 Year Investment Opportunity Just Started (Most Aren’t Ready)
eKQsjwdRrhA.creator: Tom Nash
eKQsjwdRrhA.summary: Tom Nash's macro rebuttal of Michael Burry's crash warning is the video's spine. He lays out Burry's case — the market in 'stage one of grief' (denial, ~6-9 months, so a 2027 blow-up), puts on NVDA/PLTR/MU expiring through next year — then counters with data: the S&P 500 near record highs (~7,800, 30 record closes in 2026) yet priced at a forward P/E of ~19, exactly its 10-year average, with Q3 earnings growth near 30% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth implied. He walks through the risk ledger honestly — 10-year Treasury above 5.3% (highest since 2002, but the long-run average is ~5.5% and high-rate decades delivered the best equity returns), a Fed that hiked on 16 Sep into a hot economy, and Brent near $100 driven by Iran conflict capacity loss — and concludes each risk hits unprofitable, leveraged and rate-sensitive companies hardest, which are already on his avoid list, while net-cash compounders float. On Burry's AI-bubble thesis (chip depreciation stretched over 5-6 years, $3T in off-balance-sheet hyperscaler commitments), he cites Steve Eisman's counter: a cost problem only kills if revenues stop growing, and cloud backlogs are still surging. He admits bias upfront — he owns a lot of Palantir and Burry is shorting it — and uses Burry's Jan 2023 'sell' tweet (S&P ~4,077 then, ~7,800 now) as a market-timing cautionary tale. The playbook: emergency fund, DCA as normal, trim winners 10/20/30% at +50/+100/+150%, double down only below 10% off the 52-week high (7,040 for the S&P) or 20% for big growth names like PLTR/NVDA/TSLA. No new individual stock calls; consistent with his 2 Oct SPY core-holding stance. Also promoted his 17 Oct masterclass.

H12AMJAOSE4.title: I Added $15,000 To These 3 Stocks
H12AMJAOSE4.creator: Daniel Pronk
H12AMJAOSE4.summary: Daniel Pronk walks through the three stocks he bought over the past week, calling them the best risk-reward opportunities in the market right now. First is Construction Partners (ROAD), now ~5.4% of his portfolio: the stock is down ~30% (~40% off highs) after what he saw as a strong Q3 (record revenue, ~30% YoY profit growth, record backlog, guidance raised every quarter). He rebuts the bear cases — inflation/oil costs are handled by a pass-through cost model, and higher rates barely dent $565M EBITDA vs $17.6M per 1% rate rise — and shows the stock at its cheapest P/EBITDA (~10.3x) since Sept 2020. His DCF gives FV $178 (27% CAGR, 231% 5-yr return), and even bear-case inputs (13% EBITDA growth, 12x exit) yield 15% CAGR. Second is Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), >6% of his portfolio: a 4.4% dividend targeted to grow ~15%/yr (yield-on-cost ~9% in 5 years), fwd P/E 21.7 vs 26.9 median, record 2026 fundraising, and fee-related earnings +16%/yr since 2020; he expects ~15-20% annual returns. Third is Amazon (AMZN), his second-largest position (>13%): AWS raised GPU pricing 15% on demand > supply, the chip sale-leaseback is a liquidity move for $200B+ CapEx (100+ data centers considered), and his conservative DCF gives FV $371 (~$500 by 2028, +88% 3yr). No new tickers beyond these three; Patreon/Discord pitch closes the video. Caption note: several metrics were read aloud without on-screen numbers, so DCF figures are per his narration.

6pm5KqQw6RI.title: The UNTHINKABLE is About to Happen to Stocks (but most will invest wrong)
6pm5KqQw6RI.creator: Tom Nash
6pm5KqQw6RI.summary: Tom Nash argues an exceptional setup is coming — 'one of the greatest investing opportunities of our lifetime' — but that 90% of investors will waste it for lack of a decision system. The video is framework, not stock-picking: he contends more information without a system ('brain pasta') produces noise, emotional errors, selling winners early and missing drawdown buys. He lays out his system — pre-made trim rules (take 10% at +50% gains, 20% at +100% to fund DCA/cash flow), double-down DCA (buy double when an index is 10%+ off highs or a stock 20%+ off, back to normal at 9%/20% recovery, halve DCA pace if a stock runs 20% in 30 days), and a 125-point 'no-BS' quality filter scoring cash-vs-debt, revenue growth, margins, short interest, scalability, moat, CEO, recession-proofing and secular trends (100-125 = exceptional buy, 75-100 = watchlist). Mentions as illustrations only: Palantir (his 2020-era call, +2600% realized), Nvidia (+1500% since Oct 2020), Datadog (+120% since academy addition), Bloom Energy (+80% Feb), plus his 40% PLTR / 40% S&P 500 / 20% Tesla portfolio (+565% weighted since Sept 2023). No new explicit stock calls are made — PLTR, NVDA, DDOG, BE appear as past winners, not buy/sell recommendations. Closes promoting a free live masterclass Sat Oct 17 2pm ET revealing the full system plus two new stock picks. Caption note: auto-transcript mangles company names ('Palunteer'/'Palanteer' = Palantir, 'Bloom' references = Bloom Energy).

yn_cvSds3lw.title: BE READY! Tuesday Could Change Everything for Stocks

Swhi7Bqtukg.title: Why Zeta Global Could Be a Multi-Bagger
Swhi7Bqtukg.creator: Asymmetric Investing
Swhi7Bqtukg.summary: Travis Hornsby of Asymmetric Investing follows up Zeta Live, saying he was already bullish on Zeta Global (ZETA) — it is the #2 position in the Asymmetric portfolio — and the announcements make him even more bullish long-term, with 10x potential over the next decade or more. The headline launch is Athena OS, which expands Zeta beyond its demand/marketing business (using proprietary and customer data to decide where ad spend goes across connected TV, email, SMS and social) into the supply side: matching inventory, demand and pricing and planning moves for clients, which expands the total addressable market. Athena OS is heading into beta, initially free for early users, with fixed plus variable pricing to come. Also announced: an MCP connection so clients can query Zeta data and build plans inside ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude; specialized Athena inference models built with Fireworks on Nvidia's open-model stack, fine-tuned for domain language and brand voice while keeping enterprise data proprietary — a data-sovereignty pitch he links to Palantir's Alex Karp, who appeared on stage; and custom silicon, possibly arriving around 2027. Fundamentals cited: revenue compounded at 37.6% since the March 2024 quarter with growth accelerating, operating leverage improving, management guiding growth above 20% through at least 2028 with 2028 adjusted EBITDA and free-cash-flow margin targets, and goals possibly extended to 2031/2032. Valuation: an $8.4B market cap at about 5x enterprise value to sales on a ~30% growth rate. Call made: ZETA — BUY reiterated, more bullish. One caption spot is garbled (the scaled / super-scaled customer count), so that figure is not relied on. Other tickers are mentioned only as examples or partners (Palantir, Nvidia, Nike, Gap, Lululemon), with no calls on them.

1fg4FpDs5Sg.title: AI Stocks Are Crashing...But Something BIG Is Happening!!
1fg4FpDs5Sg.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
1fg4FpDs5Sg.summary: Jose Najarro, filming while on vacation with his family, runs through a red day for semiconductors — the Korean market down roughly 6%, AMD down ~2%, Nvidia down over 1% to below $226, Credo down ~7%, Micron back in the 900s and down a further 1.4% after hours, Marvell down ~3% — and argues the news underneath is mostly bullish, though he cautions the market will stay volatile and this may not be the bottom. First, Microsoft plans to make its Maia chip its primary AI inference system with multi-gigawatt deployment from 2027: he says this is not bearish for Nvidia, whose total cost of ownership is still the best and whose demand is not dented given how much compute is needed, and it is bullish for Marvell, which he understands is part of the Maia 300 ecosystem. Second, Meta is now #3 in AI models behind only Anthropic and ahead of OpenAI and Google — extremely bullish, in his view, with the infrastructure to sell tokens at great value. Third, Taiwanese media reports that Intel, Qualcomm and AMD have raised or plan to raise CPU prices: with agentic demand far above supply, pricing restores balance and lifts margins — extremely bullish for all three; he holds AMD and is starting to look more closely at Qualcomm. Fourth, from the networking-focused semiconductor conference, Nvidia's 576-GPU scale-up/scale-out advances are very bullish for Marvell, Credo and Astera Labs. He also defends Broadcom's CEO against blame for the selloff, reading the 'casino gamblers' comments as a warning to use capital wisely rather than a bearish call, and notes Nvidia partnership updates with Meta, Google, Microsoft and Cisco as positive but not revolutionary. Calls made: MRVL, NVDA, AMD, CRDO and ALAB — BUY reiterated; META — BUY, first tracked; QCOM and INTC — UNCERTAIN, first tracked mentions. Auto-captions repeatedly garble Marvell as 'Marll' and some product names, so figures are taken from context.

PaTsaOCSUo0.title: The Next AI Revolution Is Here… THIS is the ONE Stock I'm Buying
PaTsaOCSUo0.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
PaTsaOCSUo0.summary: Joseph Hogue follows up his 9 October Robo Strategy video with a long interview with Andrew Kang, CEO of Robo Strategy — the Nasdaq-listed closed-end fund trading under ticker BOT — framing BOT in the title as the one stock he is buying for the robotics wave. Kang argues physical AI is the missing intelligence piece that now makes robotics viable: the physical labour market is a ~$50 trillion proxy, Morgan Stanley's base case is ~$5 trillion with nearly a billion humanoids, and the bottom-up math is stark — 100,000 humanoids at $50,000 is ~$5 billion of revenue, a million is ~$50 billion, ten million ~$500 billion. The portfolio spans general-purpose humanoids (Figure AI — praised for founder Brett Adcock's record, a team drawn from Boston Dynamics, Tesla and DeepMind, and unprecedented development speed), intelligent robot arms/cobots, the actuator supply chain (30–50% of a robot's bill of materials, no mature supply chain yet) and application-specific names like Path Robotics, whose AI welding business just won a $600 million contract with shipbuilder HII. On the fund itself: the closed-end structure exists because the holdings are private and long-term; NAV is marked off last financing rounds, so it lags by 12–24 months; the fund trades at a premium to NAV, and Kang's 'multiple arbitrage' engine issues shares at that premium and redeploys the cash to lift NAV per share — NAV/share is up over 50% (~55%) in about four months since launch, mostly from that mechanism rather than markups. Fees: 2.5% management fee, expense ratio slightly higher on one-time listing costs expected to compress, and no performance fee versus the VC 2-and-20 model. Bear case as discussed: manufacturing capacity is the binding bottleneck, AI timelines could slip by years, and the premium can shrink or flip. Timeline: hundreds of thousands to millions of robots in manufacturing within two years, tens to hundreds of millions by the early 2030s, homes late-2020s/early-2030s. Call made: BOT — BUY reiterated; no market price stated. Caption garbles include 'Robbo Strategy', 'Atronic/Optronic' for Apptronik and 'GBDT' for GPT, so names were sanity-checked against the 9 October video.

U9yAHwZNrnA.title: Bumble Stock Jumps 135% -- Buy or Sell NOW?
U9yAHwZNrnA.creator: Asymmetric Investing
U9yAHwZNrnA.summary: Travis Hornsby of Asymmetric Investing explains why Bumble (BMBL) has jumped about 135% in two days and why, as a shareholder, he will take the money rather than hold on. Bumble has agreed a take-private buyout — board-approved, with Blackstone affiliates and founder/CEO Whitney Wolfe Herd's affiliates backing it, Herd herself not voting and effectively being pushed out in favour of Ithaca-appointed co-CEOs Ravi Gupta and John Higgaman. Hornsby is candid that his thesis, built over roughly a year of accumulating shares, did not work as planned: revenue has fallen since late 2024, paying users on the Bumble app have dropped to about 2.1 million, and while Herd's strategy of serving fewer, more serious customers at higher prices lifted revenue per payer from about $24.80 to about $27.60 and improved free cash flow, the turnaround was slower than expected and competition has intensified — the stock was down about 30% year-to-date before the offer and is still down about 58% over three years even after the jump. What saved the position, in his telling, was buying a free-cash-flow-positive business cheaply: enterprise value to sales was about 0.5 before buyout rumours (about 1.1 now) and forward price to free cash flow about 5, which is what attracted the buyers. His decision: sell at about $5.95 rather than hold for the buyout price, giving up roughly ten cents to remove the risk that the deal falls through and the stock drops back to $2–$3, and accepting the small chance of a higher competing bid; the position ends up roughly 30–40% in profit and he will redeploy into better opportunities. Call made: BMBL — SELL (first tracked), take the buyout. Caption caution: the captions render the buyout offer as '$65 per share' at a 138% premium, which is inconsistent with the $5.95 sell price and ~10-cent gap he describes later in the same video, so the headline offer figure as captioned is garbled and not relied on.

DOldWUpT3d8.title: Nvidia $63 Billion Secret Portfolio and 18 Stocks I’m Watching
DOldWUpT3d8.creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
DOldWUpT3d8.summary: Joseph Hogue argues Nvidia's $63 billion 13F stock portfolio, $230 billion-plus of lease guarantees and $500 billion-plus financing platforms (with Apollo, BlackRock and Goldman Sachs) are not just circular-financing risk — the Wall Street Journal's Lucent comparison — but a road map to the next AI winners: follow the money and the bottlenecks Nvidia is paying to solve (optics, networking, memory, power, cooling). He ranks 18 stocks by dependence on Nvidia. Tier 1, highest dependence: CoreWeave and Nebius are his biggest question marks, Intel is a pass (foundry execution vs TSMC unproven, despite Nvidia's ~$30B stake), while Synopsys is a like — critical design software, ~37% expected revenue growth, still attractively valued. Tier 2 holds his favourite opportunities: Coherent and Lumentum on the optical bottleneck ('I'd be buying both'), Arista Networks, and Marvell, which he has been buying for a while; Nokia is rejected as legacy telecom growing only 4-7%, and SpaceX is a wait given valuation and remaining lockup expirations despite its rebound to around IPO price. Tier 3: Broadcom, Marvell and Arista can all be owned together, and Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are the safest cash-flow monsters that need no Nvidia cheque. Calls: BUY COHR, LITE, SNPS, MRVL, ANET, AVGO; AVOID INTC, NOK, ORCL; HOLD SPCX. Captions garble several names — 'Cororeweave', Coherent's ticker as 'COR', Lumentum as 'Lummentum/LIT', Nokia as 'NK' — tickers above are the companies actually discussed; no share prices are stated in the video.

WZtK2549w7Q.title: CoreWeave Stock CRASHES 15% — Here's Why I'm BULLISH!!
WZtK2549w7Q.creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
WZtK2549w7Q.summary: Jose Najarro, filming on vacation, argues the roughly 15% fall in CoreWeave (CRWV) is a buying opportunity rather than a thesis break. He says he is not worried, citing his own heavy daily AI use — increased further after recent OpenAI announcements — and ASML's earnings comment that chipmaking customers expect supply to fall short of demand until at least 2028, implying AI infrastructure providers should keep earning well. He explains the selloff through CoreWeave bond yields touching 15% and fears, sparked by Oracle asking regulators to expedite data-centre pipelines amid buildout delays, that CoreWeave could face similar delays collecting revenue. He stresses the 15% yield is the market price for existing July 2026 bonds, not what CoreWeave pays, though future debt could cost more. CoreWeave is hit hardest, he says, because it is the largest neocloud — it added 500 megawatts last quarter, more than Nebius and all other peers combined — carries the most debt, and has no other business leg to stand on, unlike the Mag 7. He also questions Elon Musk's motives in amplifying bubble warnings (SpaceX competes for customers) and sees Nvidia's $500 billion AI compute financing platform with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield and Goldman Sachs as a future funding backstop that could lower CoreWeave's financing costs. His closing valuation: 1.5 gigawatts of capacity at a ~$36 billion market cap versus ~$60 billion of value per gigawatt. Call: CRWV BUY (adding to neoclouds), no share price stated. Nebius (NBIS) and IREN, both down about 9%, are discussed as sector peers with no ticker-specific calls. Captions garble names throughout — 'Coree/Core Reef/Cororeef' for CoreWeave, 'Nebas/Nebia' for Nebius and 'Iran' for IREN.
